newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Iraq needs $30 bln investment for oil - official.
newsitem.headline: Iraq needs $30 bln investment for oil - official.

text.p: Iraq will need $30 billion to rehabilitate and further develop its dormant oil industry over a 10 year period once United Nations sanctions against it are lifted, an Iraqi official said on Tuesday.

"It is a conservative estimate that 30 billion dollars is required by the Iraqi oil industry over a period of 10 years," said Faleh Al-Khayat, Director General of Planning at the Ministry of Oil in Baghdad.

"We think approximately 15 billion will easily be obtained on a production sharing format ... if the remaining figure cannot be raised through production sharing it will be put on the national priority list."
Al-Khayat, addressing an industry conference in Nicosia, said a priority for the Iraqi government was to reach a capacity of 3.5 million barrels per day.
"The second phase is to increase capacity to 6.0 million barrels per day and sustain it in cooperation agreements with foreign companies," he said.
Iraq has been under U.N. sanctions since its August 1990 invasion of Kuwait. The trade curbs place a blanket ban on its oil exports and investments in the country.

Al-Khayat said direct government financing was preferred to develop and rehabilitate the oil industry, but said that it would be in competition with pressing civilian infrastructure projects which made foreign participation necessary.

The Iraqis have earmarked the fields of Majnoon, West Qurna (second stage), Bin Umar, Nassiriyah, Halfaya, Ratawi, Gharaf, Al-Ahdab, Tuba and Rafidain as designated to be developed by shared effort with foreign companies, Al-Khayat said.
Between them the 10 fields have an estimated production rate of 2.6 million barrels per day.
"Any foreign investment application will be handled on a case-by-case basis," he said.
Al Khayat said the current capacity of Iraq is 2.5 million barrels a day. "This can increase to 3.0 million barrels per day after a few months of lifting the embargo."
